mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about pressure is correct?

options.A: Pressure is the same as force.
options.B: Pressure is the force applied per unit area.
options.C: Pressure depends only on the mass of an object.

mcqs.answer: Pressure is the force applied per unit area.
mcqs.explanation: Pressure is defined as the magnitude of the normal force acting per unit area on a surface (P = F/A). It is measured in pascals (N/m²), not in newtons. Option B correctly states this definition, while the other options describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate pressure to force and area
mcqs.question: A force of 200 N is applied uniformly over an area of 0.5 m². What is the pressure exerted on the surface?
mcqs.explanation: Pressure is calculated using P = F/A. Substituting the given values: P = 200 N / 0.5 m² = 400 N/m² = 400 Pa. Hence option B is correct. The other options result from incorrect arithmetic.

mcqs.question: At a depth of 5 m, which fluid exerts a greater pressure on a submerged plate: water (density 1000 kg/m³) or oil (density 800 kg/m³)?

options.A: Both fluids exert the same pressure.
options.B: Water exerts a greater pressure than oil.
options.C: Oil exerts a greater pressure than water.
options.D: The pressure depends on the temperature of the fluids.

mcqs.answer: Water exerts a greater pressure than oil.
mcqs.explanation: Pressure in a fluid at depth h is given by P = ρgh. For water: P = 1000 × 9.8 × 5 = 49,000 Pa. For oil: P = 800 × 9.8 × 5 = 39,200 Pa. Since water has a higher density, it produces a larger pressure at the same depth. Option B is correct; temperature does not affect this comparison directly.

mcqs.learning_point: Apply pressure concepts to everyday situations
mcqs.question: Why does a sharp knife cut more easily than a dull knife when the same force is applied?

options.A: A sharp knife has a larger contact area with the material.
options.B: A sharp knife exerts a larger pressure on the material for the same applied force.
options.C: A sharp knife is heavier than a dull knife.
options.D: A sharp knife is made of a special metal that reduces friction.

mcqs.answer: A sharp knife exerts a larger pressure on the material for the same applied force.
mcqs.explanation: Cutting ability depends on pressure (P = F/A). A sharp knife has a very small edge area, so for a given force the pressure is high, allowing it to shear the material. Option B captures this principle. Options A, C, and D describe unrelated factors.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines thrust?

options.A: The force exerted by a fluid on a surface in contact with it.
options.B: The force that opposes the motion of an object.
options.C: The force that propels an object forward, often produced by expelling a fluid or gas.
options.D: The force due to gravity acting on a mass.

mcqs.answer: The force that propels an object forward, often produced by expelling a fluid or gas.
mcqs.explanation: Thrust is the reaction force that moves an object in the opposite direction to the expelled fluid or gas (Newton's third law). It is the principle behind rockets and jet engines. Option C correctly defines thrust; the other options describe pressure, friction, and weight respectively.

mcqs.question: Pressure is best described as:
mcqs.explanation: Pressure quantifies how much normal force is applied over a given area (P = F/A) and is measured in pascals. Option A states this definition. Options B, C, and D refer to density, hydrostatic pressure (which includes height), and velocity, respectively, and are not definitions of pressure.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate pressure to force and area
mcqs.question: Which equation correctly relates pressure (P), force (F), and area (A)?
mcqs.explanation: The fundamental relationship is P = F/A, meaning pressure equals force divided by the area over which it acts. Option B expresses this correctly. The other options are mathematically incorrect representations of the relationship.

mcqs.question: A diver descends to a depth of 10 m in freshwater (density = 1000 kg/m³). What is the gauge pressure exerted by the water at that depth? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Gauge pressure in a fluid is given by P = ρgh. Substituting: P = 1000 kg/m³ × 9.8 m/s² × 10 m = 98,000 N/m² = 98,000 Pa. Option A is correct. Option B would correspond to a depth of 1 m, while C and D are unrelated.
